provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Plant growth
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state the conditions for plant growth.
The pupils should be able to explain how plants grow from seeds.

Introduction:
We have learned about different types of plants in our class. Today we will learn what plants need to grow well.

Content:
Plants need water to grow. They need sunlight to make food. Plants need good soil to get nutrients. We can grow beans to see how they grow. Put a bean in wet cotton. Keep it in sunlight. After days, you will see a small plant growing.

Class activity:
Each pupil will plant a bean seed in a small cup with cotton. They will water it and keep it in sunlight.

Evaluation questions:
What do plants need to grow?
What happens if a plant has no water?
How long does it take for a bean to sprout?

Summary:
Plants need water sunlight and good soil to grow well.

topics.title: Animal care
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list the needs of pets and farm animals.
The pupils should be able to explain how to care for animals properly.

Introduction:
We have learned about different animals. Today we will learn how to take good care of animals.

Content:
Animals need food to eat. They need clean water to drink. Animals need shelter from the sun and rain. Pets like dogs need exercise. Farm animals like chickens need a safe place to sleep. We should be kind to all animals.

Class activity:
Pupils will draw a picture of their favorite animal and show what it needs to be healthy.

Evaluation questions:
What do animals need to stay healthy?
Why do farm animals need shelter?
How can we show kindness to animals?

Summary:
Animals need food water shelter and care to be healthy and happy.

topics.title: The human skeleton
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify major bones in the human body.
The pupils should be able to explain how joints help us move.

Introduction:
We have learned about our body parts. Today we will learn about the bones inside our body.

Content:
The skeleton is made of many bones. Our skull protects our brain. Our backbone helps us stand straight. Joints are where two bones meet. Joints allow us to bend our arms and legs. We can move because of our joints and muscles.

Class activity:
Pupils will make a simple skeleton using straws and thread to show how bones connect.

Evaluation questions:
What is the skeleton?
Name two bones in our body.
How do joints help us move?

Summary:
The skeleton gives our body shape and helps us move with the help of joints.

topics.title: Teeth and digestion
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name the four types of teeth.
The pupils should be able to explain how to care for our teeth.

Introduction:
We use our teeth every day when we eat. Today we will learn about different teeth and how to keep them clean.

Content:
We have four types of teeth. Incisors cut food like when you bite a yam. Canines tear food like meat. Premolars grind food. Molars crush food like groundnut. We should brush our teeth twice daily with a soft brush. We should eat less sugar to keep teeth healthy.

Class activity:
Pupils will draw the four types of teeth and label them correctly.

Evaluation questions:
Name the four types of teeth.
What is the use of incisors?
How should we care for our teeth?

Summary:
We have different teeth for different jobs and we must brush them daily to keep them healthy.

topics.title: Electricity basics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state safety rules for electricity.
The pupils should be able to make a simple circuit with a battery and bulb.

Introduction:
We use electricity in our homes for lights and fans. Today we will learn how to use electricity safely.

Content:
Electricity is very useful but can be dangerous. Never put water near electrical sockets. Do not touch broken wires. A battery can make a bulb light up. Connect the battery to the bulb with wires. The electricity flows from the battery through the wires to the bulb.

Class activity:
Pupils will work in groups to make a simple circuit using a battery bulb and wires to light the bulb.

Evaluation questions:
Name one safety rule for electricity.
What do we need to light a bulb with a battery?
What happens if we touch a live wire?

Summary:
Electricity is useful but we must be careful and follow safety rules when using it.

topics.title: Magnetism
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify magnetic materials.
The pupils should be able to explain what magnets can do.

Introduction:
Some materials can stick to magnets. Today we will learn about magnets and what they can do.

Content:
Magnets can attract certain materials like iron and steel. A magnet has two poles called north and south. Like poles repel each other. Unlike poles attract each other. Magnets can pick up small metal objects. We can use magnets to play games and in many machines.

Class activity:
Pupils will play a magnet fishing game using a magnet to catch paper clips from a bowl of water.

Evaluation questions:
What materials can a magnet attract?
What are the two poles of a magnet?
What happens when two north poles are brought together?

Summary:
Magnets can attract certain materials and have two poles that can either attract or repel each other.

topics.title: Water cycle
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain what evaporation is.
The pupils should be able to describe the water cycle.

Introduction:
Water changes from liquid to gas and back again. Today we will learn about the water cycle.

Content:
The sun heats water in rivers and oceans. This makes water turn into vapor. This is called evaporation. The vapor rises and cools in the sky. This forms clouds. When clouds get heavy, water falls as rain. Rain goes back to rivers and oceans. This cycle continues all the time.

Class activity:
Pupils will draw the water cycle showing evaporation cloud formation and rain.

Evaluation questions:
What is evaporation?
What happens when water vapor cools in the sky?
Where does rain go after it falls?

Summary:
The water cycle is how water moves from earth to sky and back again through evaporation and rain.

topics.title: Pollution
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name different types of pollution.
The pupils should be able to suggest ways to keep our environment clean.

Introduction:
Our environment can become dirty in different ways. Today we will learn about pollution and how to prevent it.

Content:
Air pollution happens when dirty air enters the sky. Water pollution happens when dirty things get into our rivers. Land pollution happens when we throw trash on the ground. We can keep our air clean by not burning trash. We can keep water clean by not throwing things in rivers. We should always use the dustbin.

Class activity:
Pupils will make posters showing ways to prevent pollution in our school and community.

Evaluation questions:
What is air pollution?
Name one way to keep water clean.
What should we do with our trash instead of throwing it on the ground?

Summary:
Pollution makes our environment dirty and we must all work together to keep our air water and land clean.

topics.title: Simple technology projects
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to plan a simple technology project.
The pupils should be able to build a model using simple materials.

Introduction:
We can make useful things using simple materials. Today we will learn how to make a simple technology project.

Content:
A technology project is something we make to solve a problem. We can make a model house using cardboard. We can make a toy car from plastic bottles. We need to plan what we want to make. We need to collect materials. Then we build our project step by step.

Class activity:
Pupils will work in groups to build a model of a bridge using cardboard and tape.

Evaluation questions:
What is a technology project?
What materials do we need to make a model house?
Why is it important to plan before making a project?

Summary:
We can make useful things by planning and building simple models with everyday materials.

topics.title: Revision and science fair
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall what they have learned this term.
The pupils should be able to present their science project to the class.

Introduction:
Today we will review what we have learned and show our science projects to everyone.

Content:
We have learned about plant growth animal care the skeleton teeth electricity magnets the water cycle pollution and making models. For the science fair each pupil or group will show their project. They will explain what they made and how it works. Others can ask questions about the project.

Class activity:
Pupils will present their science projects to the class during the science fair.

Evaluation questions:
What is one thing you learned this term?
What is your favorite project and why?
What question would you ask about someone else's project?

Summary:
We have learned many science concepts and now we will share our projects with others.
